subject.title: browser tool: include current page URL in before_tool_call params for act/type actions

question: Should browser `before_tool_call` handlers receive a policy-safe current tab URL for `act`/`type`, and should that contract be an injected event param or a hook-context query helper?
rationale: This changes a third-party plugin hook/security boundary: exposing too much URL state can leak sensitive browser targets, while exposing too little keeps credential-domain checks cache-based and fragile.

options.title: Add policy-safe hook URL contract
options.body: Expose a browser-owned current URL at the pre-action decision point, with policy/redaction rules and tests across supported browser profile types.

options.title: Add query helper instead of params
options.body: Keep `event.params` unchanged and add a hook context helper for browser URL lookup, reducing param mutation but expanding hook context API surface.

options.title: Keep plugin workaround only
options.body: Leave core unchanged and rely on plugins to cache URLs and fail secure, accepting repeated plugin complexity and restart-cold blocking.

recommendation.title: Add policy-safe hook URL contract
recommendation.body: Expose a browser-owned current URL at the pre-action decision point, with policy/redaction rules and tests across supported browser profile types.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent safe tab URL response work and adjacent browser route policy history make this the closest owner for choosing the browser-side contract shape.
